Theme

element noun

a basic substance: the four elements; a chemical element

also elements, the four elements, chemical element, periodic table

classical

Plin. NH 2.10
Cic. Ac. 1.26; Lucr. 1.827 (Lewis & Short)

elementum, elementī n.

noun, second declension

an element, a first principle of matter

Classically the four elements of which all things are made, fire, air, water and earth, mostly in the plural; the chemists kept the word for the elements of their table. Its other everyday senses are the letters of the alphabet and the first principles of a subject, the ABC (prīma elementa; see alphabet and basic).

Examples

  • nec dē elementīs videō dubitārī quattuor esse ea

    nor do I see any doubt that the elements are fourPlin. NH 2.10

See also basic, alphabet, chemical, science, air, fire, water.
